homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym. 'OlmoTrace' (the X card) and 'OLMOTRACE' (the ACL abstract's small capitals) are spellings of the entity. The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the tool and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: infini-gram (the index the tool extends; the census lists it as unchecked, 'infini-gram as a separate record')
the Ai2 Playground (the surface the tool runs on; unchecked in the census)
the OLMo models (OLMo 2, OLMoE, OLMo 3; the models it traces)
Dolma (named by T, by no field source; the field names olmo-mix-1124 and dolmino-mix-1124)
influence functions, TRAK and training-data attribution methods (the class's other methods: B7 §6; #725, #1075, #1714)
retrieval-augmented generation systems, Google AI Overview, Bing Chat and Perplexity among them, and Gemini's 'double-check response' (set apart by B7 §6 and B6)
the Data Provenance Initiative (the census's neighbour; its /non row is datasets/negative-of-the-negative/v2/rows/data-provenance-explorer.json, not edited)

captures.description: OLMOTRACE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an open-source system developed by the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (Ai2) that traces language model outputs back to their multi-trillion-token training datasets in real time.' How it works (the Show OLMoTrace button highlights verbatim spans; matches against corpora such as Dolma, ranking up to 10 documents by BM25; an extended infini-gram at O(L log N)), supported models (OLMo 2 32B and 13B Instruct, OLMoE 1B 7B, the OLMo 3 family), uses (fact-checking, hallucination diagnosis, auditing). Six cards: Ai2's blog, arXiv 2504.07096, the ACL Anthology, Ai2 on X (OLMo 3), Techzine, Ken Yeung's newsletter.

atoms.evidence: developed by the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (Ai2)
After a model generates a response in the Ai2 Playground, users can click the Show OLMoTrace button to highlight verbatim spans of text.
traces language model outputs back to their multi-trillion-token training datasets in real time
It uses an extended version of infini-gram
